Advanced Functional Materials | ⭐ Review
💡 This review uniquely applies molecular-level functional-group design to resolve the trilemma of ionic conductivity, electrochemical stability, and interfacial compatibility in in-situ polymerized gel electrolytes. It establishes theoretical frameworks from five dimensions and systematically links functional groups to high-voltage stability, wide-temperature operation, and intrinsic safety, providing actionable guidelines for high-energy-density, safe lithium metal batteries.

Advanced Functional Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using EMIMI as a single multifunctional additive that simultaneously stabilizes the Zn anode via interfacial EMIM⁺ adsorption (suppressing water side reactions and enabling oriented Zn (100) deposition without altering bulk solvation) and boosts cathode capacity through reversible iodine redox chemistry. Its significance is exceptional durability: over 10,000 h in symmetric cells and 84.5% capacity retention after 10,000 cycles, advancing practical AZIBs.

item.title: Synergistic Electronic‐Ionic Regulation in LMFP Cathodes Enabled by Mn‐Vacancy Engineering and D–p Orbital Hybridization
item.description:
هم‌تنظیمی Zn/Zr با مهندسی تهی‌جای Mn و هیبریداسیون اوربیتال d-p، انتقال یون و الکترون را در کاتد LMFP بهبود داده و ظرفیت و پایداری چرخه را افزایش می‌دهد.
Small | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in coupling Mn-vacancy engineering with Zn/Zr-induced d–p orbital hybridization to simultaneously boost ionic and electronic transport in LMFP cathodes. This synergistic electronic-ionic regulation lowers the band gap, enhances electron delocalization, and reduces Li⁺ diffusion barriers, yielding high capacity (156.8 mAh g⁻¹ at 0.2 C), excellent rate performance, and long cycling stability, establishing a general design strategy for olivine cathodes.
🏷 LMFP cathode · Mn vacancy · d-p orbital hybridization · lithium-ion battery · Zn/Zr doping
